lessons.title: Set your stop first
lessons.summary: Where your stop goes, and why you choose it before you buy or sell.

blocks.caption: Your entry, your stop, and the part you can lose between them.

blocks.text: A stop is the price where you get out if the trade goes against you. It keeps a bad trade small.
When you buy, you lose money if the price falls. So your stop goes below your entry.
When you sell first, you lose money if the price rises. So your stop goes above your entry.
The gap between your entry and your stop decides how much you can lose. Choose it before you trade, while you are calm, not after the price has moved.
Kairos draws the risk box on your trade picture only when the trade has a stop.

blocks.question: You buy at 100. Where does your stop go?
blocks.explanation: On a buy you lose when the price falls, so the stop sits below your entry. A stop at 100 leaves no room: the smallest dip would close the trade.

blocks.text: When you log your next trade, open Trade plan and fill in Planned stop before you save.
Or practise it first with pretend money: save a practice trade with a Planned stop.

lessons.title: How much to buy for your risk
lessons.summary: Choose the most you are willing to lose, then let your stop decide how much you can buy.

steps.title: Start with what you can lose

blocks.text: Before you buy, choose the most you are willing to lose on this one trade. Many traders choose 1% of their account or less.
Each coin you buy can lose the gap between your entry and your stop. Divide what you are willing to lose by that gap: that is how much you can buy.
Move the stop further away and you can buy less. The loss at the stop stays the same.

blocks.question: Your stop moves further from your entry. What happens to how much you can buy?
blocks.explanation: Each coin can now lose more, so fewer coins fit inside the amount you chose to lose.

blocks.text: Work out a trade of your own, with your own numbers.

lessons.title: Read your trade picture
lessons.summary: What the boxes, the candles and the result on your trade picture mean.

blocks.text: Every trade in your Journal has a picture: your plan drawn as boxes, and your entries and exits as marks.
The box between your entry and your stop is the part you can lose. The box between your entry and your target is the part you can win.
Planned reward compares the two boxes. 2× means the part you can win is twice as big as the part you can lose.
Behind the boxes are the candles from the time of your trade. With no internet connection, the picture shows only your plan and your entries and exits.
Result after fees is what the trade really made or lost. Actual result compares it with what you planned to lose: +2× means you won twice that.

blocks.question: Your trade picture says +2× what you risked. What happened?

choices.text: You won twice what you planned to lose
You doubled all the money in your account
You lost twice what you planned to lose

blocks.explanation: × what you risked compares your result with the loss you planned at your stop, not with all the money in your account.

blocks.text: Open the Journal and tap the small picture on a trade card to see your own trade.
Or replay a past market: place a practice trade and watch its picture grow, one candle at a time.
